data.headline: Enjoying Retirement (for now)
data.about:
I am a technologist with over two decades of experience creating online worlds and the technology platforms that support them. I have grown through the ranks, from hands on engineer and architect to an engineering leader capable of establishing a vision and hiring and directing top notch industry talent.

One of the founding members of Turbine, I led the development of the company's technology platform, including Turbine's MMO game engine and back-end service platforms, building everything from highly scalable rendering engines, content creation tools, fault tolerant server back-ends, international e-commerce systems, customer service tools, and much more.

After the acquisition of Turbine by Warner Bros., I led the development of a back-end technology platform intended to be used by multiple studios across Warner Bros.

After 2 years at Warner Bros., I left to take a "sabbatical" and travel the world for a year; however, gaming is my passion and I took a role at Epic Games working on some amazing new opportunities there.

I lead the development of Epic’s online platforms, including UE Marketplace, Fortnite, and Epic Games store, Epic Online Services, and more.

After successfully managing the explosive growth of Fortnite, I am now enjoying some time off although I expect I will decide to work again someday.

description.text:
I have been taking a "sabbatical" to fulfill my lifelong dream to travel the world.  While traveling, doing volunteer work for various NGOs and other organizations became a focus of my time.

Area of travel include:
• Road trip across the USA covering 16+ national parks and other sites along the way
• 6 month stay in Hawaii visiting all the different islands and living on Maui for many months
• 2 month trip to Africa including visits to South Africa, Zimbabwe, Zambia, and Uganda
• Trip to Turkey to visit Istanbul and other areas of this rich-history country

While on Maui, I volunteered for two organizations.  First, the Hawaii Wildlife Fund (http://wildhawaii.org), where learned about specific conservation issues facing Hawaii and helped out with many of the programs they offer.  Second, for the State of Hawaii, working in Ahihi-Kinau Natural Area Reserve, helping to educate visitors on conservation issues at this much visited park.  While in Uganda, I volunteered with Connect Africa (http://connect-africa.org), a community-based organization that helps underprivileged children with educational needs.

Turbine was acquired by Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment (WBIE) in May 2010. Although I was still at Turbine, which became a studio of WBIE, my role extended to working on back-end technologies and consumer facing websites across all of WBIE, supporting multiple game titles and development studios worldwide - a project code-named WBNet.

I drove the green light for WBNet, working with finance, legal, production, marketing, and other departments at the WBIE publishing group, before presenting to senior executives for final budget approval.

During the course of WBNet development, I directly led the development team at Turbine and worked closely with multiple WBIE studios and the publishing group of WBIE in Burbank to create detailed plans for the development and roll out of this new publishing platform.

I was part of the team of entrepreneurs that formed Turbine over a decade ago with the vision of becoming a leading provider of online entertainment. Before being acquired by Warner Bros., Turbine had grown to over 350 employees and became one of the largest privately-held online gaming studios in North America. Turbine has created some of the most popular gaming worlds on the Internet, like the award-winning Asheron's Call, Dungeons & Dragons Online, and The Lord of the Rings Online.

As CTO, I established the vision and led the engineering team who built Turbine's state-of-the-art massively multiplayer online engine and supporting tools and technology, using both in-house proprietary and 3rd party developed technologies. During my career, I have worked as hands-on coder, software architect, scrum master, project manager, executive leader, and in many other roles as needed to make Turbine a success. In addition to directly managing the core technology team at Turbine, I established HR, engineering, and software development best practices across all of Turbine's development teams. I also worked across other Turbine departments to understand their requirements and build better tools and technology to support business operations.

I was hands on managing technical aspects of Turbine's 3rd party relationships. I worked closely with international partners to launch Turbine's games in Europe, China, Korea, Japan, and Russia, and with technology vendors to integrate 3rd party technologies into Turbine's platform.

As a member of the executive team, I was point on presenting Turbine's publishing platform to potential investors and acquirers. I worked closely with finance to manage the development budget for my team and closely with the rest of the executive team to create a development roadmap for Turbine's technology platform.
